sentences.zh: 孔崇弼，初仕後唐，自吏部郎中授給事中，時族兄昭序繇給事中改左常侍，兄弟同居門下，時論榮之。

translations.literal: Kong Chongbi at first served Later Tang; from Director in the Ministry of Personnel he was appointed Supervising Censor. At the time his clansman elder brother Zhaoxu changed from Supervising Censor to Left Regular Attendant. The brothers both served together in the Gate and Attendant Office, and contemporary opinion held it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chongbi began his career under Later Tang, rising from director in the Ministry of Personnel to supervising censor. About then his elder clansman Zhaoxu moved from supervising censor to left regular attendant, so the two brothers served together in the Gate and Attendant Office—a pairing that contemporaries regarded as a mark of distinction.

sentences.zh: 崇弼，天福中遷左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Chongbi, in the Tianfu era, was transferred to Left Irregular Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu reign period Chongbi was promoted to left irregular cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 無他才，但能談笑，戲玩人物，揚眉抵掌，取悅於人。

translations.literal: He had no other talent but could jest and chat, sport with people's characters, raise his brows and clap his palms, and please others.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed no other ability, but he could banter and jest, mock and toy with people, lift his brows and clap his hands together, and win others' favor.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔令泛海使於杭越。

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict ordered him to go by sea as envoy to Hang and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the reign he was ordered by edict to sail as envoy to Hang and Yue.

sentences.zh: 先是，浙中贈賄，每歲恒及萬緡，時議者曰：「孔常侍命奇薄，何消盈數，有命即無財，有財即無命。

translations.literal: Earlier, gifts and bribes from Zhejiang each year regularly reached ten thousand strings of cash. Commentators of the time said: "Supervisor Kong's fate is strangely thin—how could he consume such a full sum? If he has life he has no wealth; if he has wealth he has no life."
translations.idiomatic: Previously, presents and bribes from Zhejiang had routinely amounted to ten thousand strings of cash a year. People at the time remarked, "Supervisor Kong's fate is peculiarly meager—how could he ever enjoy such a windfall? Where there is life there is no money; where there is money there is no life."

sentences.zh: 」明年使還，果海中船壞，空手而歸。

translations.literal: " The next year the envoy returned; indeed the ship was wrecked at sea, and he came back empty-handed.
translations.idiomatic: " The following year the envoy returned, and as predicted the ship was lost at sea; he came home with nothing.

translations.idiomatic: Here an editorial opening bracket appears in the text.

sentences.zh: （案：以下殘闕。）〉

sentences.zh: 陳保極，閩中人也。

translations.literal: Chen Baoji was a man of Minzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baoji was a native of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 好學，善屬文，後唐天成中擢進士第，秦王從榮聞其名，辟為從事。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was skilled at literary composition. In the Tiancheng era of Later Tang he passed the jinshi examination. Prince of Qin Congrong heard his name and recruited him as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was studious and skilled at composition. In the Tiancheng period of Later Tang he passed the jinshi examination, and when Prince of Qin Congrong heard of him he took him on as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 從榮素急暴，後怒保極不告出遊宰相門，以馬箠鞭之，尋出為定州推官。

translations.literal: Congrong was by nature impetuous and violent. Later he grew angry that Baoji had gone out to visit a chief minister's gate without informing him, and beat him with a horse whip; soon afterward he was sent out as investigating officer of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Congrong was naturally hot-tempered and violent. Later he flew into a rage because Baoji had gone calling on a chief minister without telling him, and lashed him with a horsewhip; before long Baoji was posted out as investigating officer in Ding prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從榮敗，執政知其屈，擢居三署，歷禮部、倉部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Congrong was defeated, those in power knew he had been wronged and promoted him to the Three Bureaus, where he served successively as vice director in the Ministries of Rites and of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After Congrong's defeat the authorities recognized that Baoji had been treated unjustly and promoted him into the Three Bureaus, where he served in succession as vice director in the ministries of Rites and of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 初，桑維翰登第之歲，保極時在秦王幕下，因戲謂同輩曰：「近知今歲有三個半人及第。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the year Sang Weihan passed the examination, Baoji was then on the Prince of Qin's staff. In jest he said to his colleagues: "I have just learned that this year three and a half men passed."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the year Sang Weihan passed the jinshi examination, Baoji was serving on the Prince of Qin's staff. He joked to his colleagues, "I've just heard that three and a half men passed this year."

sentences.zh: 」蓋其年收四人，保極以維翰短陋，故謂之半人也。

translations.literal: " For that year four men were admitted; Baoji, because Weihan was short and homely, therefore called him half a man.
translations.idiomatic: " That year four candidates were admitted, but because Weihan was short and plain-looking, Baoji counted him as only half a man.

sentences.zh: 天福中，維翰既居相位，保極時在曹郎，慮除官差跌，心不自安，乃乞假南遊，將謀退跡。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era, once Weihan had taken the chief ministership, Baoji was then a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue. Fearing that his appointment might be demoted, he was ill at ease in mind and asked leave to travel south, intending to withdraw from office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu period, after Weihan had become chief minister, Baoji was serving as a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue. Fearful that his post might be downgraded, he grew uneasy and asked leave to travel south, planning to retire from public life.

sentences.zh: 既而襄、鄧長吏以行止入奏，維翰乃奏於高祖曰：「保極閩人，多狡，恐逃入淮海。

translations.literal: Soon the senior officials of Xiang and Deng reported his conduct to the throne. Weihan then memorialized to Emperor Gaozu: "Baoji is a man of Min, very crafty; I fear he may flee into the Huaihai region."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the senior officials of Xiang and Deng reported his movements to court. Weihan then memorialized Emperor Gaozu, saying, "Baoji is a Fujianese and notoriously cunning; I fear he may flee to the Huaihai region."

sentences.zh: 」即以詔追赴闕，將下臺鍛成其事，同列李崧極言以解之，因令所司就所居鞫之，貶為衛尉寺丞，仍奪金紫。

translations.literal: " An edict at once recalled him to the capital. They were about to send him down to the censorate to forge the case into a crime, but his colleague Li Song spoke forcefully in his defense. Thereupon the authorities were ordered to interrogate him at his residence; he was demoted to assistant director of the Court of Imperial Regalia and also stripped of his gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict immediately recalled him to the capital. The censorate was about to manufacture a case against him, but his colleague Li Song argued strenuously on his behalf. The authorities were then ordered to try him at his home; he was demoted to assistant director of the Court of Imperial Regalia and stripped of his gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 尋復為倉部員外郎，竟以銜憤而卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was restored as vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, but in the end he died nursing resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, but in the end he died still brooding over the wrong done him.

sentences.zh: 保極無時才，有傲人之名，而性復鄙吝，所得利祿，未嘗奉身，但蔬食而已。

translations.literal: Baoji had no talent for his times and bore a reputation for arrogance toward others; moreover his nature was mean and stingy. The salary and emoluments he received he never spent on himself—only plain vegetables for food.
translations.idiomatic: Baoji had no real talent for his age and was known for looking down on others; he was also miserly by nature. He never spent his salary and stipends on himself and ate only plain fare.

sentences.zh: 每與人奕棋，敗則以手亂其局，蓋拒所賭金錢不欲償也。

translations.literal: Whenever he played chess with others and lost, he would scramble the board with his hand—clearly refusing to pay the wagered money.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he played chess and lost, he would sweep the pieces about with his hand—an obvious ploy to avoid paying what he had wagered.

sentences.zh: 及卒，室無妻兒，帷囊中貯白金十鋌，為他人所有，時甚嗤之。

translations.literal: When he died his household had no wife or children. In a curtain pouch were stored ten ingots of white silver belonging to someone else, and people of the time greatly ridiculed him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he left no wife or children. In a pouch in his curtains were ten ingots of white silver that belonged to someone else, and contemporaries mocked him roundly for it.

sentences.zh: 王瑜，其先范陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yu—his ancestors were men of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu's family originally came from Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 父欽祚，仕至殿中監，出為義州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Qinhuo served up to Director of the Palace Domestic Service and went out as prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qinhuo rose to director of the palace domestic service and was then posted out as prefect of Yi.

sentences.zh: 瑜性兇狡，然雋辯驍果，騎射刀筆之長，亦稱於當代。

translations.literal: Yu was by nature fierce and cunning, yet he was eloquent, brave, and resolute; his skill in horsemanship, archery, and the brush also won praise in his generation.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was fierce and treacherous by nature, yet he was eloquent, bold, and resolute, and his prowess in horsemanship, archery, and the written arts also won renown in his day.

sentences.zh: 起家累為從事。

translations.literal: From his first appointment he repeatedly served as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career with successive appointments as staff officer.

sentences.zh: 天福中，授左贊善大夫。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era he was appointed Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu period he was appointed left mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 會濮郡秋稼豐衍，稅籍不均，命乘使車，按察定計。

translations.literal: It happened that in Pu prefecture the autumn harvest was abundant but the tax registers were uneven; he was ordered to ride the envoy carriage and inspect and fix the assessments.
translations.idiomatic: When Pu prefecture enjoyed a bountiful autumn harvest but its tax registers were uneven, he was sent out in the envoy carriage to inspect the district and set the levies aright.

sentences.zh: 既至郡，謂校簿吏胡蘊、惠鶚曰：「余食貧久矣，室無增資，為我致意縣宰，且求假貸。

translations.literal: When he reached the prefecture he said to the registry clerks Hu Yun and Hui E: "I have been poor in food for a long time and my household has no added resources. Convey my regards to the district magistrates and ask them for loans."
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the prefecture he told the registry clerks Hu Yun and Hui E, "I have been poor for a long time and my household has no extra income. Pass word to the district magistrates for me and ask them for loans."

sentences.zh: 」由是濮之部內五邑令長共斂錢五十萬，私獻於瑜。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the magistrates of the five districts within Pu together collected five hundred thousand in cash and privately presented it to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: " The magistrates of the five districts within Pu then pooled five hundred thousand cash and privately presented it to Yu.

sentences.zh: 瑜即以書上奏，高祖覽章嘆曰：「廉直清慎有如此者，誠良臣也。

translations.literal: Yu at once memorialized in writing. Emperor Gaozu read the memorial and sighed: "Integrity, uprightness, purity, and caution such as this—truly a fine minister."
translations.idiomatic: Yu immediately submitted a memorial. When Emperor Gaozu read it he exclaimed, "Integrity, uprightness, purity, and caution such as this—truly a fine minister."

sentences.zh: 」於是二吏五宰即時停黜，擢瑜為太府少卿。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the two clerks and five magistrates were at once dismissed, and Yu was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: " The two clerks and five magistrates were dismissed on the spot, and Yu was promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 杜重威之鎮東平也，瑜父欽祚為節度副使，及重威移鎮常山，瑜乃詭計於重威，使奏己為恒州節度副使，竟代其父位。

translations.literal: When Du Chongwei governed Dongping, Yu's father Qinhuo was deputy military governor. When Chongwei was transferred to garrison Changshan, Yu devised a ruse with Chongwei so that he memorialized for Yu himself as deputy military governor of Hengzhou, and in the end Yu replaced his father's post.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Chongwei held Dongping, Yu's father Qinhuo served as his deputy military governor. After Chongwei was transferred to Changshan, Yu tricked him into memorializing for Yu himself as deputy military governor of Heng, and in the end Yu took his father's place.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，入為刑部郎中。

translations.literal: After more than a year he entered the capital as director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year he was recalled to the capital as director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 丙午歲，父欽祚刺舉義州，瑜歸寧至郡。

translations.literal: In the bingwu year his father Qinhuo was investigating and reporting on Yizhou; Yu returned home on leave to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingwu year his father Qinhuo was serving as investigating commissioner in Yi prefecture, and Yu went home on leave to visit him there.

sentences.zh: 會契丹據有中夏，何建以秦州歸蜀，瑜說欽祚曰：「若不西走，當屬契丹矣！

translations.literal: It happened that the Khitan held the Central Plains; He Jian surrendered Qinzhou to Shu. Yu urged Qinhuo: "If we do not flee west, we shall fall to the Khitan!"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan had seized the Central Plains, and He Jian had surrendered Qin to Shu. Yu urged his father, "If we do not flee west, we shall end up under the Khitan!"

sentences.zh: 」厲色數諫，其父怒而不從。

translations.literal: " With stern countenance he remonstrated repeatedly; his father grew angry and would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: " He remonstrated again and again with a fierce expression, but his father grew angry and refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 因其臥疾涉旬，瑜仗劍而脅之曰：「老懦無謀，欲趨炮烙。

translations.literal: Because he had lain ill for more than ten days, Yu drew his sword and threatened him: "Old coward without a plan—you wish to rush toward the brazier torment!"
translations.idiomatic: When his father had been bedridden for more than ten days, Yu drew his sword and threatened him: "You feeble old fool with no plan—you mean to march straight into the torturer's fire!"

sentences.zh: 不即為計，則死於刃下。

translations.literal: If you do not decide at once, you die beneath the blade."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not act now, you die by this blade."

sentences.zh: 」父不得已而聽之。

translations.literal: " His father had no choice but to comply.
translations.idiomatic: " His father had no choice but to yield.

sentences.zh: 時隴東屯兵扼其川路，將北趣蕃部假途，而因與郡盜酋長趙徽歃血為約，以兄事之。

translations.literal: At the time Longdong garrison troops blocked the river routes; they intended to go north toward the tribal lands to borrow a passage, and therefore with the bandit chieftain of the prefecture, Zhao Hui, they swore blood brotherhood and treated him as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Longdong garrison troops then blocked the river routes, so they planned to head north through the tribal lands to borrow a passage. Yu therefore swore a blood oath with the bandit chieftain Zhao Hui of the prefecture and treated him as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 謂徽曰：「西至成都，余身為相，余父為將，爾當領一大郡，能遂行乎？

translations.literal: He said to Hui: "When we reach Chengdu westward, I myself shall be chief minister and my father a general; you shall hold a great prefecture. Can you carry this through?"
translations.idiomatic: He told Hui, "When we reach Chengdu in the west, I shall become chief minister and my father a general, and you shall govern a great prefecture. Will you go through with this?"

sentences.zh: 」徽曰：「諾。

translations.literal: " Hui said: "Agreed."
translations.idiomatic: " Hui said, "Agreed."

sentences.zh: 」瑜慮為所賣，先致其妻孥，館於郡中。

translations.literal: " Yu feared being betrayed and first sent his wife and children ahead, lodging them in the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: " Fearing betrayal, Yu first sent his wife and children ahead and lodged them in the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 行有期矣，徽潛召其黨，伺於郊外。

translations.literal: The day of departure was set. Hui secretly summoned his followers and lay in wait in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: When the day of departure was fixed, Hui secretly gathered his men and waited in ambush outside the city.

sentences.zh: 子夜，瑜舉族行，輜重絡繹十有餘里。

translations.literal: At midnight Yu moved with his whole clan; baggage trains stretched in an unbroken line for more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight Yu set out with his entire clan, their baggage trains trailing for more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 徽之所親，循溝澮而遁，至馬峽路隅，舉燧相應，其黨起於伏莽，斷欽祚之首，貫諸長矛。

translations.literal: Hui's intimates fled along the ditches and canals; when they reached a corner of the road at Maxia they raised beacon fires in answer. His followers rose from ambush in the thickets, severed Qinhuo's head, and impaled it on long spears.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's confederates slipped along ditches and canals until they reached a bend on the road at Maxia, where they lit signal fires. His men sprang from ambush in the brush, cut off Qinhuo's head, and spitted it on long spears.

sentences.zh: 平生聚蓄金幣萬計，皆為賊所掠，少長百口，殺之殆盡。

translations.literal: Gold and coin he had amassed over a lifetime, numbering in the tens of thousands, were all plundered by the bandits. Of young and old, more than a hundred mouths, nearly all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The gold and coin he had amassed over a lifetime—tens of thousands in all—were plundered by the bandits. Of more than a hundred people, young and old alike, nearly all were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 瑜尚獨戰千人，矢不虛發，手無射捍，其指流血。

translations.literal: Yu still fought alone against a thousand men; not an arrow missed. He had no thumb guard for shooting, and his fingers bled.
translations.idiomatic: Yu still fought alone against a thousand men, and every arrow found its mark. He had no archer's thumb guard, and his fingers ran with blood.

sentences.zh: 及窘，乃夜竄山谷，落發為僧。

translations.literal: When hard pressed, he fled by night into the mountain valleys, shaved his head, and became a monk.
translations.idiomatic: When he was cornered, he fled by night into the mountains, shaved his head, and became a monk.

sentences.zh: 月餘，為樵人所獲，縶送岐州，為侯益所殺，時年三十九。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was seized by woodcutters, bound, and sent to Qizhou, where Hou Yi had him executed. He was thirty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month woodcutters captured him, bound him, and sent him to Qi prefecture, where Hou Yi had him executed. He was thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 始瑜有姑寡居，來歸其家，以前夫遺腹有子，經數年不產，每因事預告人吉兇，無不驗者。

translations.literal: From the first Yu had an aunt who lived as a widow; she came to join his household. Her former husband's posthumous child was said to be in her womb, yet for several years she did not give birth. Whenever events arose she foretold people's fortune or misfortune, and without exception it came true.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had an aunt who lived as a widow and came to live in his household. She was said to be carrying her late husband's posthumous child, yet for years she bore none. Whenever something happened she would foretell people's fortune or misfortune, and her predictions always came true.

sentences.zh: 時契丹入中闕，前月餘謂瑜曰：「暴兵將至，宜速去之，茍不去，亂必及矣。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered the central capital, more than a month before she told Yu: "Violent troops are coming—you should flee quickly. If you do not leave, disorder will surely reach you."
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered the central capital, more than a month earlier she had told Yu, "Violent troops are coming—you should flee at once. If you do not leave, calamity will overtake you."

sentences.zh: 」後瑜果死，此謂「天作孽，猶可違；

translations.literal: " Later Yu indeed died. This illustrates the saying: "When Heaven brings calamity, it may still be defied;
translations.idiomatic: " Yu did indeed die afterward. This illustrates the saying, "When Heaven brings calamity, one may still defy it;

sentences.zh: 自作孽，不可逭」也。

translations.literal: when one brings calamity on oneself, it cannot be escaped."
translations.idiomatic: but when one brings calamity on oneself, there is no escape."

sentences.zh: 張繼祚，故齊王全義之子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jizuo was the son of the former Prince of Qi, Zhang Quanyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jizuo was a son of the former Prince of Qi, Zhang Quanyi.

sentences.zh: 始為河南府衙內指揮使，全義卒，除金吾將軍，旋授蔡州刺史，累官至檢校太保。

translations.literal: At first he was commander of the Henan prefectural guard; when Quanyi died he was appointed general of the Golden Wu Guard, soon made prefect of Caizhou, and rose in office to Grand Guardian with honorary title.
translations.idiomatic: He began as commander of the Henan prefectural guard. After Quanyi's death he was appointed general of the Golden Wu Guard, soon made prefect of Cai, and eventually rose to honorary grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 明宗郊天，充供頓使，復除西衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong performed the suburban sacrifice to Heaven, he served as provisioning commissioner and was again appointed general of the Western Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong performed the suburban sacrifice to Heaven, Jizuo served as provisioning commissioner and was again appointed general of the Western Guard.

sentences.zh: 唐清泰末，丁母憂。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang's Qingtai reign he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Qingtai reign of Tang he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 天福初，喪制未闋，會張從賓作亂，發兵迫脅，取赴河陽，令知留守事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, before his mourning period had ended, Zhang Congbin rebelled; troops were sent to coerce him, he was taken to Heyang, and ordered to act as regent of the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianfu period, before his mourning term had ended, Zhang Congbin rebelled. Troops were sent to coerce Jizuo, who was taken to Heyang and ordered to serve as regent of the garrison.

sentences.zh: 從賓敗，與二子詔戮於市。

translations.literal: When Congbin was defeated, he and his two sons were executed by edict in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: When Congbin was defeated, he and his two sons were executed by imperial order in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 始繼祚與範延光有舊，嘗遣人以馬遺之。

translations.literal: From the first Jizuo had old ties with Fan Yanguang and once sent someone to present him with horses.
translations.idiomatic: Jizuo had long been on friendly terms with Fan Yanguang and once sent him horses as a gift.

sentences.zh: 屬朝廷起兵，將討鄴城，為巡兵所獲，奏之，高祖深忌之。

translations.literal: When the court raised troops to campaign against Yecheng, the gift was seized by patrol soldiers and reported; Emperor Gaozu deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: When the court raised an army to attack Yecheng, patrol troops seized the gift and reported it, and Emperor Gaozu took deep offense.

sentences.zh: 及敗，宰臣桑維翰以父珙早事齊王，奏欲雪之，高祖不允，

translations.literal: When he was defeated, the chief minister Sang Weihan, because his father Gong had long served the Prince of Qi, memorialized to clear the family, but Emperor Gaozu would not agree,
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat, chief minister Sang Weihan—whose father Gong had long served the Prince of Qi—memorialized to clear the family's name, but Emperor Gaozu refused,

translations.literal: (The Zizhi Tongjian: Li Tao, reviser of the Historiography Institute, memorialized: Zhang Quanyi had the merit of restoring Luoyang; he begged that the clan be spared.)
translations.idiomatic: (The Zizhi Tongjian: Li Tao, reviser of the Historiography Institute, memorialized that Zhang Quanyi had restored Luoyang and asked that his clan be spared.)

translations.literal: Thereupon the execution of Jizuo's wife and children was halted.) Right angle bracket closes the insertion.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the execution of Jizuo's wife and children was halted.)

sentences.zh: 遂止罪繼祚一房，不累其族。

translations.literal: Thereupon punishment was limited to Jizuo's own household and did not extend to the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment was then limited to Jizuo's own household and did not extend to the wider clan.

sentences.zh: 胡饒，大梁人也。

translations.literal: Hu Rao was a man of Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Rao was a native of Daliang.

sentences.zh: 少事本鎮連帥為都吏，歷馬步都虞候。

translations.literal: In youth he served the local military governor of his circuit as chief clerk and successively held the post of commander of horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served the circuit military governor as chief clerk and later held the post of commander of horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 會唐明宗鎮其地，與部將王建立相善，明宗即位，建立領常山，奏饒為真定少尹。

translations.literal: When Tang Emperor Mingzong governed that region he was on good terms with the staff general Wang Jianli. When Mingzong took the throne, Jianli held Changshan and memorialized for Rao as vice prefect of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong of Tang governed the region, Rao was on good terms with staff general Wang Jianli. After Mingzong took the throne, Jianli held Changshan and recommended Rao as vice prefect of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 饒本憸人，既在府幕，無士君子之風。

translations.literal: Rao was by nature a treacherous man; once in the governor's staff he had none of a gentleman's bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Rao was treacherous by nature, and once he entered the governor's staff he showed none of a gentleman's conduct.

sentences.zh: 嘗因事趙郡，有平棘令張鵬者獻策，請建立於境內每縣所管鄉置鄉直一人，令月書縣令出入行止，饒乃導而薦焉。

translations.literal: Once on business in Zhao commandery there was the magistrate of Pingji, Zhang Peng, who offered a plan: he asked Jianli to place one village inspector in each township under every district in the territory, ordering them each month to record the magistrate's comings and goings. Rao guided and recommended it.
translations.idiomatic: Once while on business in Zhao commandery, Zhang Peng, magistrate of Pingji, proposed that Jianli appoint one village inspector in each township under every district, with monthly reports on the magistrates' movements. Rao promoted the scheme.

sentences.zh: 建立行之彌年，詞訟蜂起，四郡大擾。

translations.literal: Jianli carried it out for more than a year; lawsuits swarmed like bees and the four commanderies were greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Jianli implemented it for more than a year, lawsuits multiplied, and the four commanderies were thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 天成末，王都構亂，陰使結建立為兄弟之國。

translations.literal: At the end of Tiancheng, Wang Du plotted rebellion and secretly sent envoys to ally with Jianli as brother states.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tiancheng period Wang Du plotted rebellion and secretly sent envoys to ally with Jianli as brother states.

sentences.zh: 時饒又曾薦梁時右庶子張澄為判官，建立亦狎之。

translations.literal: At the time Rao had also recommended Zhang Cheng, former right mentor of the heir under Liang, as administrative aide; Jianli was likewise intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Rao had also recommended Zhang Cheng, former right mentor of the heir under Liang, as administrative aide, and Jianli was equally fond of him.

sentences.zh: 澄素不知書，每座則以《陰府》、《鬼谷》為己任。

translations.literal: Cheng by nature did not know books; whenever he took a seat he made the Yin Fu and Guiguzi his business.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was illiterate by nature and at every gathering treated the Yin Fu and Guiguzi as his specialty.

sentences.zh: 建立時密以王都之盟告之，澄與饒俱贊成其事，會王師圍中山，其事遂寢，而饒之兇戾如此。

translations.literal: Jianli at the time secretly told them of Wang Du's alliance; Cheng and Rao both approved the affair. When the imperial army besieged Zhongshan the matter was dropped, yet Rao's ferocity and violence were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Jianli secretly told them of Wang Du's alliance, and both Cheng and Rao endorsed it. When the imperial army besieged Zhongshan the plot collapsed, but Rao's savagery was of this sort.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，馮道出鎮同州，饒時為副使，道以重臣，稀於接洽，饒忿之，每乘酒於牙門詬道，道必延入，待以酒肴，致敬而退。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, Feng Dao went out to govern Tongzhou; Rao was then deputy commissioner. Because Dao was a great minister he rarely received visitors; Rao resented this and, whenever drunk, would revile Dao at the headquarters gate. Dao always invited him in, entertained him with wine and food, paid his respects, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qingtai period Feng Dao was posted to govern Tong, with Rao as his deputy. As a senior minister Dao rarely received visitors, which angered Rao, who when drunk would curse him at headquarters. Dao always invited him in, served wine and food, paid his respects, and let him leave.

sentences.zh: 道謂左右曰：「此人為不善，自當有報，吾何怒焉。

translations.literal: Dao said to those beside him: "This man does evil; he will have his recompense of himself—why should I be angry?"
translations.idiomatic: Dao told his attendants, "This man does evil; he will bring retribution on himself—why should I be angry?"

sentences.zh: 」饒後閑居河陽。

translations.literal: " Later Rao lived in retirement at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Rao lived in retirement at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 天福二年夏，會張從賓作亂，饒謁於麾下，請預其行。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu, summer, Zhang Congbin rebelled; Rao called on him under his banner and asked to join the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second Tianfu year Zhang Congbin rebelled. Rao presented himself to Congbin and asked to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 從賓敗，饒以王建立方鎮平盧，走投之，建立延入城，斬之以聞，聞者快焉。

translations.literal: When Congbin was defeated, Rao, because Wang Jianli was then military governor of Pinglu, fled to him. Jianli welcomed him into the city, beheaded him, and reported it; those who heard rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: When Congbin was defeated, Rao fled to Wang Jianli, who was then military governor of Pinglu. Jianli welcomed him into the city, beheaded him, and reported the deed; those who heard of it were delighted.

sentences.zh: 劉遂清，字得一，青州北海人，梁開封尹鄩之猶子也。

translations.literal: Liu Suiqing, courtesy name Deyi, was a man of Beihai in Qingzhou, a nephew by marriage of Zheng, chief minister of the capital under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Suiqing, courtesy name Deyi, was from Beihai in Qing prefecture and was a nephew by marriage of Zheng, Liang's chief minister of the capital.

sentences.zh: 父琪，以鴻臚卿致仕。

translations.literal: His father Qi retired as director of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi had retired as director of the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 遂清少敏惠，初仕梁為保鑾軍使，歷內諸司使，莊宗入汴，不改其職。

translations.literal: Suiqing from youth was quick and clever. He first served Liang as commissioner of the Palace Guard, held successive posts as commissioner of the inner bureaus, and when Zhuangzong entered Bian his offices were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Suiqing was clever from youth. He first served Liang as commissioner of the palace guard, held successive posts as commissioner of the inner bureaus, and when Zhuangzong entered Bian his offices were left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，加檢校尚書僕射，委以西都監守。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he was given the honorary title Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and entrusted with guarding the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne he was given the honorary title of vice director of the Masters of Writing and entrusted with guarding the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，以中山王都有不臣之跡，除遂清為易州刺史，俾遏其寇沖，既至郡，大有禦侮之略，境內賴焉。

translations.literal: After more than a year, because Wang Du of Zhongshan showed signs of disloyalty, Suiqing was appointed prefect of Yizhou to check his raids. Once he reached the prefecture he had great strategies for defense, and the territory relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, when Wang Du of Zhongshan showed signs of disloyalty, Suiqing was appointed prefect of Yi to block his raids. On reaching the prefecture he devised strong defenses, and the region came to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 王都平，加檢校司空，遷棣州刺史。

translations.literal: When Wang Du was pacified he was given the honorary title Minister of Works and transferred to prefect of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Du was pacified he was given the honorary title of minister of works and transferred to prefect of Li.

sentences.zh: 天成、長興中，歷典淄、興、登三郡，咸有善政。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng and Changxing he successively governed the three prefectures of Zi, Xing, and Deng, and in all had good administration.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng and Changxing periods he governed in succession the prefectures of Zi, Xing, and Deng, and in each he administered well.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒潞王紀》：帝之起鳳翔也，召興州刺史劉遂清，遲疑不至。

translations.literal: (The Zizhi Tongjian, Annals of the Prince of Lu: When the emperor rose at Fengxiang he summoned Liu Suiqing, prefect of Xingzhou; hesitating, he did not come.)
translations.idiomatic: (The Zizhi Tongjian, Annals of the Prince of Lu: When the emperor rose at Fengxiang he summoned Liu Suiqing, prefect of Xing, but Suiqing hesitated and did not come.)

sentences.zh: 聞帝入洛，乃悉集三泉、西縣、金牛、桑林戍兵以歸，自散關以南，城鎮悉棄之，皆為蜀人所有。

translations.literal: Hearing that the emperor had entered Luoyang, he then gathered all the garrison troops of Sanquan, Xixian, Jinniu, and Sanglin to return. From San Pass southward, cities and towns were all abandoned and came into Shu possession.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that the emperor had entered Luoyang, he gathered all garrison troops from Sanquan, Xixian, Jinniu, and Sanglin and withdrew. From San Pass southward he abandoned every city and town, and all fell to Shu.

translations.literal: When he entered court the emperor wished to punish him, but because he had returned of his own accord he was pardoned.) Right angle bracket closes the insertion.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court the emperor wished to punish him, but because he had returned of his own accord he was pardoned.)

sentences.zh: 高祖即位之二年，授鳳州防禦使，加檢校司徒，會丁母憂，起復，授內客省使、右監門衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gaozu's reign he was appointed defense commissioner of Fengzhou and given the honorary title Grand Master. When he entered mourning for his mother he was recalled from mourning and appointed commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau and great general of the Right Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gaozu's reign he was appointed defense commissioner of Feng and given the honorary title of grand master. When his mother died he was recalled from mourning and appointed commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau and great general of the Right Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 六年，駕幸鄴都，轉宣徽北院使兼判三司，加檢校太保。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when the emperor visited Yedu, he was transferred to commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently judged the Three Bureaus, and given the honorary title Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when the emperor visited Yedu, he was transferred to commissioner of the northern bureau of the palace secretariat with concurrent charge of the Three Bureaus, and given the honorary title of grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 七年，少帝嗣位，加右領軍衛上將軍，仍賜竭誠翊戴保節功臣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the Young Emperor succeeded, he was made general of the Right Army Guard and also granted the title of Meritorious Minister of Loyal Support and Preservation of Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the Young Emperor succeeded, he was made general of the Right Army Guard and granted the title of Meritorious Minister of Loyal Support and Preservation of Integrity.

sentences.zh: 八年，出領鄭州，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he went out to govern Zhengzhou and was given the honorary title Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was posted to govern Zheng and given the honorary title of grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 開運二年，遷安州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun he was transferred to defense commissioner of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyun he was transferred to defense commissioner of An.

sentences.zh: 未幾，上表稱疾，詔許就便，回至上蔡，終於郵舍，時三年四月也。

translations.literal: Before long he memorialized claiming illness; an edict permitted him to return at convenience. On the way back he reached Shangcai and died at a post station—it was the fourth month of the third year.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he memorialized that he was ill; an edict allowed him to return at his convenience. On the way back he reached Shangcai and died at a post station, in the fourth month of the third year.

sentences.zh: 遂清性至孝，牧淄川日，自北海迎其母赴郡，母既及境，遂清奔馳路側，控轡行數十里，父老觀者如堵，當時榮之。

translations.literal: Suiqing was by nature supremely filial. While governing Zichuan he went from Beihai to welcome his mother to the prefecture. When his mother had reached the border, Suiqing ran along the roadside, holding the reins and walking several tens of li. The elders who watched were packed like a wall, and people of the time honored it.
translations.idiomatic: Suiqing was profoundly filial by nature. While governing Zichuan he went from Beihai to bring his mother to the prefecture. When she reached the border, he ran along the roadside holding the reins and walked with her carriage for several tens of li. The elders who watched lined the road, and contemporaries praised the deed.

sentences.zh: 遂清素不知書，但多計畫，判三司日，每給百官俸料，與判官議曰：「斯輩非盡有才能，多世祿之家，宜澄其汙而留其清者。

translations.literal: Suiqing by nature did not know books, but he had many schemes. While judging the Three Bureaus, whenever he issued the officials' salaries he would discuss with his administrative aides: "These people do not all have ability; many are hereditary salary families. The tainted should be cleared away and the clean retained."
translations.idiomatic: Suiqing was illiterate by nature but full of schemes. While in charge of the Three Bureaus, whenever he issued officials' salaries he would tell his aides, "These men are not all capable—many come from hereditary salary families. We should sift out the corrupt and keep the upright."

sentences.zh: 」或對曰：「昔唐朝渾、郭、顏、段，每一赦出，以一子出身，率為常制，且延賞垂裕，為國美譚，未有因月給而欲沙汰，恐未當也。

translations.literal: " Someone replied: "In former times under Tang, the Hun, Guo, Yan, and Duan clans—whenever an amnesty was issued one son would enter office; this was regularly the established rule. Moreover it extended rewards and left abundance, a fine tale for the state. Never has anyone wished to sift out men because of monthly pay—I fear it would not be fitting."
translations.idiomatic: " Someone replied, "Under Tang the Hun, Guo, Yan, and Duan families regularly saw one son enter office with each amnesty—that was established custom. It spread reward and left abundance, a celebrated state policy. No one has ever tried to purge men over monthly salaries; I fear that would be inappropriate."

sentences.zh: 」群論由此減之。

translations.literal: " The group's discussion thereby diminished it.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was dropped after this discussion.

sentences.zh: 劉繼勛，衛州人也。

translations.literal: Liu Jixun was a man of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jixun was a native of Wei prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐天成中，高祖鎮鄴都，繼勛時為客將，高祖愛其端謹，籍其名於帳下，從歷數鎮。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era of Tang, when Emperor Gaozu governed Yedu, Jixun was then a guest general. Gaozu loved his steadiness and care, registered his name in his staff, and took him through several garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng period of Tang, when the future Emperor Gaozu held Yedu, Jixun served as a guest general. Gaozu admired his steadiness and care, enrolled him in his personal staff, and took him through several postings.

sentences.zh: 及即位，擢為閣門使，出為淄州刺史，遷澶州防禦使，俄改鄭州，自宣徽北院使拜華州刺史。

translations.literal: When he took the throne Jixun was promoted to commissioner of the Gate and Attendant Office, sent out as prefect of Zizhou, transferred to defense commissioner of Canzhou, soon changed to Zhengzhou, and from commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat was appointed prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne Jixun was promoted to commissioner of the Gate and Attendant Office, then posted as prefect of Zi, transferred to defense commissioner of Can, soon moved to Zheng, and from commissioner of the northern palace secretariat bureau was appointed prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，鎮同州。

translations.literal: After more than a year he governed Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year he was posted to govern Tong.

sentences.zh: 始少帝與契丹絕好，繼勛亦預其謀，及契丹主至闕，繼勛自鎮來朝，契丹責之。

translations.literal: From the first, when the Young Emperor broke with the Khitan, Jixun also took part in the plot. When the Khitan ruler reached the capital, Jixun came from his garrison to court and the Khitan reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor broke with the Khitan, Jixun had taken part in the plot. When the Khitan ruler reached the capital, Jixun came from his post to court, and the Khitan reproached him.

sentences.zh: 時馮道在側，繼勛事急，指道曰：「少帝在鄴，道為首相，與景延廣謀議，遂致南北失歡。

translations.literal: Feng Dao was then at his side. Jixun, in his urgency, pointed at Dao and said: "When the Young Emperor was at Ye, Dao was chief minister and deliberated with Jing Yanguang, thereby causing North and South to lose harmony."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao stood beside him. In his panic Jixun pointed at Dao and said, "When the Young Emperor was at Ye, Dao was chief minister and plotted with Jing Yanguang, which is what brought North and South to estrangement."

sentences.zh: 臣位至卑，未嘗措言，今請問道，道細知之。

translations.literal: My post was extremely low; I never put in a word. Now I ask that Dao be questioned—Dao knows the details."
translations.idiomatic: My rank was too low for me to speak. Question Dao—he knows every detail."

sentences.zh: 」契丹主曰：「此老子不是好鬧人，無相牽引，皆爾輩為之。

translations.literal: " The Khitan ruler said: "This old fellow is not one to make trouble—do not drag him in. You lot did it all."
translations.idiomatic: " The Khitan ruler said, "This old man is no troublemaker—do not drag him into it. You people did all of this."

sentences.zh: 」繼勛不敢復對。

translations.literal: " Jixun dared not reply again.
translations.idiomatic: " Jixun dared not answer again.

sentences.zh: 繼勛時有疾，契丹主因令人候其疾狀，雲有風痹，契丹主曰：「北方地涼，居之此疾可愈。

translations.literal: Jixun was then ill. The Khitan ruler had someone inquire into his condition; it was reported that he had wind paralysis. The Khitan ruler said: "The northern lands are cool; living there this illness can be cured."
translations.idiomatic: Jixun was ill at the time. The Khitan ruler sent someone to inquire after his condition and was told he had rheumatic paralysis. The Khitan ruler said, "The north is cool; if he lives there the illness may clear."

sentences.zh: 」乃命鎖繼勛。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Jixun shackled.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered Jixun put in chains.

sentences.zh: 尋解之，以疾終於家。

translations.literal: Soon he was released and died of illness at home.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon released and died of illness at home.

translations.idiomatic: (The Zizhi Tongjian: When the Khitan ruler heard that Zhao Zaili was dead, he released Jixun, who died of grief and anger.)

translations.literal: When Han Emperor Gaozu entered Bian, he was posthumously granted Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaozu of Han entered Bian, Jixun was posthumously granted grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 唐宰相餘慶之曾孫也。

translations.literal: He was the great-grandson of Tang chief minister Yuqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was the great-grandson of the Tang chief minister Yuqing.

sentences.zh: 余慶生浣，浣生從讜，兩為太原節度使，再登相位。

translations.literal: Yuqing begot Huan; Huan begot Congdan, who twice was military governor of Taiyuan and twice reached the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing's son was Huan; Huan's son was Congdan, who twice served as military governor of Taiyuan and twice reached the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 從讜兄處誨，為汴州節度使。

translations.literal: Congdan's elder brother Chuhui was military governor of Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Congdan's elder brother Chuhui was military governor of Bian.

sentences.zh: 家襲清儉，深有士風，中朝禮法，以鄭氏為甲。

translations.literal: The family inherited purity and frugality and had deep scholar-gentleman bearing; in court ritual and law the Zheng clan ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: The family maintained purity and frugality and bore a deep scholar-gentleman's air; in court ritual and propriety the Zheng clan ranked first.

sentences.zh: 處誨生受益。

translations.literal: Chuhui begot Shouyi.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhui was Shouyi's father.

sentences.zh: 受益亦以文學致身，累歷臺閣，自尚書郎遷右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Shouyi likewise rose through literary learning, served repeatedly in the censorate and secretariat, and from director in the Masters of Writing was transferred to right remonstrance adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi likewise rose through scholarship, served repeatedly in the censorate and secretariat, and was promoted from director in the Masters of Writing to right remonstrance adviser.

sentences.zh: 天福七年夏，以張彥澤數為不道，上章請行國典，旬日不報。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventh year of Tianfu, because Zhang Yanzhe had repeatedly acted against the Way, he memorialized asking that the national statutes be applied; for ten days there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the seventh Tianfu year, because Zhang Yanzhe had repeatedly committed outrages, Shouyi memorialized asking that the national law be applied; for ten days there was no response.

sentences.zh: 又貢表切言，訐直無所忌，執政稍惡之。

translations.literal: He again presented a memorial speaking bluntly, impeaching and speaking straight without reserve; those in power gradually disliked him.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial speaking bluntly, impeaching without fear; the authorities gradually turned against him.

sentences.zh: 俄而以病請告，歸長安。

translations.literal: Soon he asked leave on grounds of illness and returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked leave on grounds of illness and returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖晏駕，以不赴國哀停任，會赦，拜京兆少尹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu died, he was suspended from office for failing to attend the national mourning; when an amnesty came he was appointed vice prefect of the capital district.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu died, Shouyi was suspended for failing to attend the national mourning; after an amnesty he was appointed vice prefect of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 宰相趙瑩出鎮鹹秦，以受益朝班舊僚，眷待甚至。

translations.literal: Chief minister Zhao Ying went out to govern Xianqin; because Shouyi was an old colleague from court he treated him with exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: When chief minister Zhao Ying was posted to govern Xianqin, he treated Shouyi, an old court colleague, with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 屬天下率借金谷，乃謂瑩曰：「京兆戶籍登耗，民力虛實，某備知之矣，品而定之，可使平允。

translations.literal: When the realm was levying grain loans everywhere, he said to Ying: "The capital district's household registers, gains and losses, and the people's strength, empty or full—I know them all in detail. Grade and fix them and fairness can be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: When the realm was levying grain loans everywhere, he told Ying, "I know the capital district's household registers, gains and losses, and the people's real capacity in full. Grade and fix them and the levies can be made fair."

sentences.zh: 」瑩信之，因使與王人同掌其事。

translations.literal: " Ying trusted him and therefore had him jointly manage the affair with Wang Ren.
translations.idiomatic: " Ying trusted him and had him manage the affair jointly with Wang Ren.

sentences.zh: 受益既經廢棄，薄於仕宦，遂阿法射利，冀為生生之資；

translations.literal: Shouyi, having already been cast aside, was indifferent to office; he therefore bent the law to seek profit, hoping for a living's resources;
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi, already cast aside from office, cared little for public service and bent the law for profit, hoping to secure a livelihood;

sentences.zh: 又素恃門望，陵轢同幕，內奸外直，群情無相洽者。

translations.literal: moreover he had long relied on his family's standing, bullied colleagues on the staff, was treacherous within and straight without—among the group none were on good terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: and he had long relied on his family's standing, bullied colleagues on the staff, and was treacherous within while appearing upright without, so that none on the staff were on good terms with him.

sentences.zh: 及贓汙事發，騰於眾口，瑩不得已，遂按之，其直百萬。

translations.literal: When the bribery affair broke out it spread on everyone's lips; Ying had no choice and investigated; the value was a million.
translations.idiomatic: When the bribery scandal broke it spread everywhere; Ying had no choice but to investigate, and the sum came to a million cash.

sentences.zh: 八年冬，賜死於家。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eighth year he was granted death at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eighth year he was ordered to take his own life at home.

sentences.zh: 受益數世公臺，一朝自棄，士君子皆惜之。

translations.literal: Shouyi's family for several generations had stood on the high terrace of state; in a single morning he cast himself away, and scholar-gentlemen all lamented it.
translations.idiomatic: The Zheng family had served at the highest levels for generations; in a single morning Shouyi threw it all away, and men of cultivation lamented it.

sentences.zh: 程遜，字浮休，壽春人。

translations.literal: Cheng Xun, courtesy name Fuxiu, was a man of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xun, courtesy name Fuxiu, was from Shouchun.

translations.literal: A left angle bracket opens an editorial insertion in the received text.
translations.idiomatic: Here an editorial opening bracket appears in the text.

sentences.zh: （案：此下有闕文。）〉

translations.literal: (Editor's note: Text is missing below this point.) Right angle bracket closes the insertion.
translations.idiomatic: (Editor's note: Text is missing below this point.)

sentences.zh: 召入翰林充學士，自兵部侍郎承旨授太常卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned into the Hanlin as academician, and from vice minister of War and bearer of edicts was appointed director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the Hanlin as an academician and promoted from vice minister of War and bearer of edicts to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 天福三年秋，命使吳越，

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Tianfu he was ordered as envoy to Wuyue,
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the third Tianfu year he was ordered as envoy to Wuyue,

translations.literal: A left angle bracket opens an editorial insertion in the received text.
translations.idiomatic: Here an editorial opening bracket appears in the text.

sentences.zh: （《十國春秋》云：禮部尚書程遜為加恩使。）〉

translations.literal: (The Spring and Autumn of the Ten States states: Minister of Rites Cheng Xun served as envoy of added grace.) Right angle bracket closes the insertion.
translations.idiomatic: (The Spring and Autumn of the Ten States states that Minister of Rites Cheng Xun served as envoy of added grace.)

sentences.zh: 母羸老雙瞽，遜未嘗白執政以辭之。

translations.literal: His mother was frail and old and blind in both eyes; Xun had never told those in power to decline the mission on that account.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was frail, elderly, and blind in both eyes, yet Xun had never asked the authorities to excuse him from the mission on her account.

sentences.zh: 將行，母以手捫其面，號泣以送之。

translations.literal: When he was about to depart, his mother felt his face with her hands and wailed as she sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to leave, his mother felt his face with her hands and wailed as she sent him off.

sentences.zh: 仲秋之夕，陰暝如晦，遜嘗為詩曰：「幽室有時聞雁叫，空庭無路見蟾光。

translations.literal: On a mid-autumn evening the gloom was dark as night. Xun once wrote a poem: "In the secluded room one sometimes hears wild geese calling; in the empty courtyard there is no path to see the moon's light."
translations.idiomatic: On a mid-autumn evening the sky was dark as night. Xun once wrote a poem: "In the secluded room wild geese sometimes cry; in the empty courtyard no path leads to the moonlight."

sentences.zh: 」同僚見之，訝其詩語稍異。

translations.literal: " Colleagues who saw it were surprised that the poem's language was somewhat strange.
translations.idiomatic: " Colleagues who read it were struck by how strange the lines sounded.

sentences.zh: 及使回，遭風水而溺焉。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he met wind and water and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey he was caught in wind and waves and drowned.

sentences.zh: 李郁，字文緯，唐之宗屬也。

translations.literal: Li Yu, courtesy name Wenwei, was of Tang imperial clan kin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, courtesy name Wenwei, was a member of the Tang imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 少歷宗寺官，天成、長興中，累遷為宗正卿。

translations.literal: In youth he passed through offices of the clan temple; during Tiancheng and Changxing he was repeatedly promoted to director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served in the clan temple offices; during the Tiancheng and Changxing periods he rose in succession to director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 性平允，所歷無愛憎毀譽。

translations.literal: His nature was even and fair; in the posts he held there was neither favoritism nor slander.
translations.idiomatic: He was even-tempered and fair-minded, and in every post he held he inspired neither favoritism nor slander.

sentences.zh: 高祖登極，授光祿卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne he was appointed director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he was appointed director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 一日晝寢，夢食巨棗，覺而有疾，謂其親友曰：「嘗聞『棗』字重『來』，呼魂之象也。

translations.literal: One day he napped by day, dreamed of eating a huge jujube, woke ill, and said to his kin and friends: "I have heard that the character for 'jujube' contains the character for 'come'—a sign of calling back the soul."
translations.idiomatic: One day he napped and dreamed of eating an enormous jujube. When he woke he was ill and told his kin and friends, "I have heard that the character for 'jujube' contains the character for 'come'—a sign that the soul is being summoned back."

sentences.zh: 余神氣逼抑，將不免乎！

translations.literal: My spirit is pressed down—I shall not escape, shall I!"
translations.idiomatic: My spirit feels crushed—I suppose I shall not escape death!"

sentences.zh: 」天福五年夏卒。

translations.literal: " In the summer of the fifth year of Tianfu he died.
translations.idiomatic: " He died in the summer of the fifth Tianfu year.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 馬重績，字洞微。

translations.literal: Ma Zhongji, courtesy name Dongwei.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhongji, courtesy name Dongwei.

sentences.zh: 少學數術，明太一、五紀、八象、三統大歷，居於太原。

translations.literal: From youth he studied numerology and was versed in the Taiyi, Five Records, Eight Images, and Santong Great Calendar; he lived in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied numerology and mastered the Taiyi, Five Records, Eight Images, and Santong Great Calendar, and he lived in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 仕晉，拜太子右贊善大夫，遷司天監。

translations.literal: He served Jin, was appointed right mentor of the heir, and was transferred to director of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: He served Jin, was appointed right mentor of the heir apparent, and was then made director of the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 天福三年，重績上言：「歷象，王者所以正一氣之元，宣萬邦之命，而古今所記，考審多差。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianfu, Zhongji memorialized: "The calendar and celestial signs are what kings use to rectify the origin of the single qi and proclaim the mandate to the myriad states, yet what is recorded from ancient times to the present, on careful examination, has many discrepancies."
translations.idiomatic: In the third Tianfu year Zhongji memorialized, "Calendars and celestial observations are how kings rectify the origin of cosmic order and proclaim the mandate to the myriad states, yet records from antiquity to the present, when examined closely, contain many errors."

sentences.zh: 《宣明》氣朔正而星度不驗，《崇元》五星得而歲差一日。

translations.literal: The Xuanming [calendar]'s qi and new moons are correct but the star degrees do not check; the Chongyuan [calendar] gets the five planets but the year differs by a day.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanming calendar's qi and new moons are correct but its star positions fail verification; the Chongyuan calendar tracks the five planets but its year is off by a day.

sentences.zh: 以《宣明》之氣朔，合《崇元》之五星，二歷相參，然後符合。

translations.literal: Take the Xuanming's qi and new moons and combine them with the Chongyuan's five planets; when the two calendars are cross-referenced, then they accord.
translations.idiomatic: Combine the Xuanming calendar's qi and new moons with the Chongyuan calendar's five planets, and only when the two calendars are cross-referenced do they agree.

sentences.zh: 自前世諸歷，皆起天正十一月為歲首，用太古甲子為上元，積歲愈多，差闊愈甚。

translations.literal: From former ages all calendars have taken the eleventh month of the celestial standard as year-head and used the primordial jiazi as superior origin; the more years accumulate, the greater the discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Calendars since antiquity have all taken the eleventh month as the year's beginning and used the primordial jiazi cycle as the superior origin; the more years accumulate, the wider the error grows.

sentences.zh: 臣輒合二歷，創為新法，以唐天寶十四載乙未為上元，雨水正月中氣為氣首。

translations.literal: Your servant has combined the two calendars and created a new method, taking the yiwei year of Tang Tianbao fourteen as superior origin and the mid-qi of the first month of Rain Water as qi-head.
translations.idiomatic: I have combined the two calendars and devised a new method, taking the yiwei year of Tang Tianbao 14 as the superior origin and the mid-qi of the first month of Rain Water as the beginning of qi reckoning.

sentences.zh: 」詔下司天監趙仁琦、張文皓等考核得失，仁琦等言：「明年庚子正月朔，用重績歷考之，皆合無舛。

translations.literal: " An edict was sent down to Zhao Renqi, Zhang Wenhao, and others of the Directorate of Astronomy to examine gains and losses. Renqi and the rest said: "Next year, the new moon of the first month of the gengzi year—checked against Zhongji's calendar, all accord without error."
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered Zhao Renqi, Zhang Wenhao, and others at the Directorate of Astronomy to evaluate the proposal. They reported, "For the new moon of the first month of next year, the gengzi year, Zhongji's calendar matches in every respect without error."

sentences.zh: 」乃下詔班行之，號《調元曆》。

translations.literal: " An edict was then issued to promulgate it; it was titled the Tiaoyuan Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict was then issued to promulgate it under the name Tiaoyuan Calendar.

sentences.zh: 行之數歲輒差，遂不用。

translations.literal: After it was used for several years discrepancies soon appeared, and it was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: After a few years in use it began to drift, and it was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 重績又言：「漏刻之法，以中星考晝夜為一百刻，八刻六十分刻之二十為一時，時以四刻十分為正，此自古所用也。

translations.literal: Zhongji also said: "The method of clepsydra graduations takes the culminating star to measure day and night as one hundred ke; eight ke and twenty sixtieth-ke make one double-hour; the double-hour takes four ke and ten [minutes] as correct—this has been used since antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongji also said, "The clepsydra method measures day and night as one hundred ke by the culminating star; eight ke plus twenty sixtieth-ke make one double-hour, and the double-hour is reckoned from four ke and ten parts—this is the ancient usage."

sentences.zh: 今失其傳，以午正為時始，下侵未四刻十分而為午，由是晝夜昏曉，皆失其正，請依古改正。

translations.literal: Now the transmission is lost; they take noon as the start of the double-hour and push down into wei by four ke and ten to make noon, whereby day and night, dusk and dawn, all lose their correctness. I ask that it be corrected according to antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: The tradition has been lost; the current practice takes noon as the start of the double-hour and encroaches four ke and ten into wei to define noon, so that day and night, dusk and dawn, are all wrong. I ask that it be corrected according to the ancient method."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " His request was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 重績卒年六十四。

translations.literal: Zhongji died at the age of sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongji died at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 陳元，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Chen Yuan was a man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuan was a native of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 家世為醫，初事河中王重榮。

translations.literal: His family for generations were physicians; at first he served Wang Chongrong of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been physicians for generations; he first served Wang Chongrong of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，後唐武皇自太原率師攻王行瑜，路出於蒲中，時元侍湯藥，武皇甚重之。

translations.literal: In the Qianfu era the Martial Emperor of Later Tang led troops from Taiyuan to attack Wang Xingyu; the route passed through Puzhong. Yuan then attended him with medicines and decoctions, and the Martial Emperor greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianfu period the Martial Emperor of Later Tang led troops from Taiyuan against Wang Xingyu, passing through Puzhong. Yuan attended him with medicines, and the Martial Emperor held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 及還太原，日侍左右。

translations.literal: When he returned to Taiyuan he attended him daily at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to Taiyuan, Yuan attended him daily at his side.

sentences.zh: 武皇性剛暴，樂殺人，無敢言者。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor was by nature fierce and violent, delighted in killing people, and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: The Martial Emperor was fierce and violent by nature, delighted in killing, and none dared remonstrate with him.

sentences.zh: 元深測其情，每有暴怒，則從容啟諫，免禍者不一，以是晉人深德之，勛貴賂遺盈門。

translations.literal: Yuan deeply gauged his moods; whenever there was violent anger he would calmly remonstrate, and those spared calamity were not few. For this the people of Jin deeply thanked him, and meritorious nobles' gifts filled his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan read his moods closely; whenever the emperor flew into a rage Yuan would calmly remonstrate, and many were spared death thereby. The people of Jin were deeply grateful, and gifts from nobles filled his gate.

sentences.zh: 性好酒樂施，隨得而無私積。

translations.literal: His nature loved wine and delighted in giving; whatever he received he did not hoard privately.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and delighted in giving away whatever came to him, never hoarding for himself.

sentences.zh: 明宗朝，為太原少尹，入為太府卿。

translations.literal: In Emperor Mingzong's reign he was vice prefect of Taiyuan and entered the capital as director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mingzong he served as vice prefect of Taiyuan, then entered the capital as director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 長興中，集平生所驗方七十五首，並修合藥法百件，號曰《要術》，刊石置於太原府衙門之左，以示於眾，病者賴焉。

translations.literal: During Changxing he collected seventy-five prescriptions he had verified in his lifetime, together with a hundred methods of compounding medicines, titled Essential Methods, carved them on stone, and placed them to the left of the Taiyuan prefectural yamen gate to show the public; the sick relied on them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing period he compiled seventy-five prescriptions he had tested in his lifetime along with a hundred methods of compounding medicines, titled Essential Methods, had them carved on stone, and set the stele to the left of the Taiyuan prefectural gate for all to see; the sick benefited from them.

sentences.zh: 天福中，以耄期上表求退，以光祿卿致仕，卒於晉陽，年八十餘。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era, on account of advanced age he memorialized asking to retire and left office as director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; he died at Jinyang at over eighty years.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu period, citing his great age, he memorialized to retire and left office as director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; he died at Jinyang in his eighties.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫彰善癉惡，《麟史》之為義也；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: To make good manifest and evil hateful is the meaning of the Lin History;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: To make good manifest and evil hateful is the purpose of the Spring and Autumn Annals;

sentences.zh: 瑜不掩瑕，虹玉之為德也。

translations.literal: not to conceal flaws is the virtue of rainbow jade.
translations.idiomatic: and not to conceal flaws is the virtue of rainbow jade.

sentences.zh: 故自崇弼而下，善者既書之，其不善者亦書之，庶使後之君子見善如不及，見惡如探湯也。

translations.literal: Therefore from Chongbi downward, what was good has been written, and what was not good has also been written, in the hope that later gentlemen, seeing good, will be as if unable to reach it, and seeing evil, will be as if testing boiling water.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore from Chongbi onward we have recorded the good and also recorded the bad, so that later gentlemen, seeing good, may strive to match it, and seeing evil, may shrink from it as from scalding water.

sentences.zh: 至如重績之曆法，陳元之醫道，亦不可漏其名而弗紀也。

translations.literal: As for Zhongji's calendrical method and Chen Yuan's medical art, their names likewise cannot be omitted and left unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: As for Zhongji's calendrical science and Chen Yuan's medical art, their names too must not be omitted from the record.
